messages:
Sofia Ivanova: posting ADR-0147 for arch review. focus: mixed workload scheduler prototype (short/interactive vs long/prefill-heavy). main trade-off in ADR is SRPT-ish vs 2-queue priority + fairness window.

Sofia Ivanova: link (internal): https://confluence.redwood/adr/0147-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy

Sofia Ivanova: explicit questions:
1) do we buy SRPT-like (predict prefill cost) given prediction error?
2) are fairness bounds in 2-queue enough for Dedicated where we have strict p95 SLOs?
3) any concerns w/ customer tier hints interacting w/ queueing?

Confluence Bot: Sofia Ivanova shared “ADR-0147: Short/Long prompt-aware scheduling policy (draft)”

Noah Patel: skimmed. overall 👍 on moving off FIFO, but i want to be careful about “SRPT approximation” language. the second you say SRPT people assume theoretical properties you won’t have.

Noah Patel: the core concern: you don’t know service time, you’re predicting prefill cost from prompt length + maybe a stub. prediction error + batching makes it *not* SRPT.

Lena Fischer: yeah, agree. in the ADR we tried to be explicit: SRPT-like only as an alternative considered. proposed prototype is 2-queue with aging/fairness.

Noah Patel: ok. then focus on 2-queue policy. i want to see the fairness contract written as something verifiable:
- max additional wait for long class under steady arrival of short
- or min long service share over window W

Noah Patel: “we’ll periodically service long” isn’t enough; it turns into tuning folklore.

Marcus Reed: current sketch is “short-first, but after N short dispatches or T ms since last long, take a long (if present)”. N/T configurable.

Marcus Reed: also considering token-based budget per class so long gets at least X% of prefill tokens over a sliding window.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to having something you can alert on. SRE POV: need a concrete starvation definition (e.g., long_queue_wait_p99 < bound, or long_queue_age_max < bound).

Sean Gallagher: if we can’t define a hard bound, at least define rollback triggers that catch “long starvation” before it becomes a customer-visible incident.

Omar El-Sayed: instrumentation plan includes:
- queue_depth{class}
- wait_time_hist{class}
- service_time split prefill/decode per class
- “last_long_dispatch_age” gauge

Omar El-Sayed: we can derive “long service share” from tokens_per_class metrics (prefill tokens ideally).

Noah Patel: good. the other thing i’m worried about is customer-tier hints.

Noah Patel: ADR mentions “maybe incorporate tier/route priority later”. i’d strongly prefer: v1 policy depends ONLY on request cost characteristics (prompt len/prefill) and not customer tier.

Noah Patel: mixing tier into scheduler is where you accidentally create “noisy neighbor *by design*”. also complicates correctness when tenants share GPU pools.

Lauren Bishop: from product side: Dedicated customers will ask for “priority” at some point, but i’m aligned w/ not mixing that into this prototype.

Lauren Bishop: we can gate by deployment mode/pool: e.g., enable flag only on Dedicated pools where we control tenancy.

Benji Okafor: +1. also feature flag config becomes a mess if we let per-customer priority leak into runtime scheduling logic. keep it clean: “policy=short_long_v1” and knobs.

Peter Holtz: fairness/tier note: if we ever do tier, it should be at admission/routing layer (separate pools / separate queues per tenant) not “tier-based priority” inside one queue.

Peter Holtz: otherwise when overloaded you’ll page SRE because “low tier long prompts never finish” and there’s no clear contract.

Noah Patel: exactly.

Hiro Tanaka: kernel-side observation: prefill is the cost driver, but actual prefill time can vary based on kernel selection + sequence length + kv cache state.

Hiro Tanaka: if you classify purely on prompt tokens, you will misclassify edge cases (e.g., short prompt + large batch -> still heavy; long prompt but cached prefix -> light).

Hiro Tanaka: just make sure the classifier can be conservative and has a “unknown” path (treat as long) to avoid short queue pollution.

Lena Fischer: we have “unknown -> long” in heuristics doc. plus we’re adding EWMA of observed prefill to refine thresholds later (but behind a guardrail).

Noah Patel: ok but note: “unknown -> long” protects short queue, but increases long queue load; need to ensure long doesn’t become a garbage bin.

Sofia Ivanova: agree. plan is conservative classification initially + tune threshold using perf suite + canary.

Paula Mendes: rollout/flag: if we’re default-off, can we also enforce “only enabled on specific routes/pools” so we don’t accidentally apply to shared multi-tenant Hosted API?

Benji Okafor: yes. config primitive supports scoping by cluster/pool and route tags. we can enforce via config validation (reject enablement on shared pools unless allowlisted).

Talia Benson: capturing action items for ADR update:
1) write fairness contract explicitly (metric + bound + how validated)
2) clarify v1 excludes customer-tier hints (only cost-based classification)
3) add note re: admission/routing as the right layer for tier separation

Noah Patel: one more: trade-off vs SRPT-like should include the batching interaction.

Noah Patel: SRPT assumes single job server; our server is “continuous batching + prefill/decode phases”. you can have a long prefill batch block short prefill even if you try SRPT at request level.

Marcus Reed: yep, we already hit something like that in load test: short got stuck behind long prefill batch. we’re adding a regression test + ensuring scheduler can preempt batch formation.

Sean Gallagher: that’s a key point for rollout readiness. add an explicit “priority inversion” guardrail + metric so oncall can see it (e.g., short_queue_wait spikes while long_prefill_batch_size grows).

Omar El-Sayed: we can expose “batch_prefill_tokens” and “batch_origin_class” on sampled structured logs. should help debug.

Hiro Tanaka: also be careful about “preemption” at kernel boundary. you can’t preempt inside a kernel; you can only choose what to launch next. so fairness windows must be in terms of dispatch opportunities, not wall time inside GPU.

Lena Fischer: makes sense. we’ll phrase it as “dispatch-level fairness” and measure it via queue wait.

Noah Patel: ok. overall: i’m 👍 on 2-queue with explicit fairness + no tier in v1. if ADR is updated with the above, i’ll sign off.

Sofia Ivanova: awesome, thanks all. i’ll update ADR today + ping for final review. :thumbsup:

Lauren Bishop: +1. once updated, i’ll reference it in Dedicated SLO comms so we don’t overpromise.

Sean Gallagher: please include SRE rollback triggers in ADR appendix (even if also in runbook). helps future readers.

Sofia Ivanova: will do.
